name: The Summoner's Circle
realm: Glowing sigils pulse. What you summon, you must also banish.
lesson: new allocates memory on the heap and returns a pointer; every new needs a matching delete (new[] needs delete[]) or you leak. Modern C++ avoids raw new: unique_ptr has exactly one owner and frees automatically; shared_ptr counts owners and frees when the last one goes. Create them with make_unique / make_shared.
lessonCode:
auto u = make_unique<int>(5);   // sole owner
auto s = make_shared<int>(7);   // shared
auto s2 = s;                    // use_count() == 2
// no delete needed - RAII cleans up

trial.prompt: Every new must be paired with…
Which header provides unique_ptr and shared_ptr?
Why can't a unique_ptr be copied?
options: a) it has exactly one owner
d) copying is only for arrays

trial.explain: Both a and b share ownership.

trial.prompt: Which line creates a unique_ptr<int> holding 9?

options: a) memory that was allocated but never freed
b) reading past an array end
boss.explain: Leaks pile up until the program exits.

boss.prompt: After unique_ptr<int> b = std::move(a); what does a hold? (one word)

spell.prompt: Write unique_ptr<int> make(int v) that returns a unique_ptr owning v.
